source_interpretation.title: Core growth and assembly are different procedures
source_interpretation.text: The two metal preparations differ in solvent and ligand timing: Au uses toluene and dodecanethiol after reduction, while Ag uses chloroform and dodecanethiol before borohydride. Film conditions use preformed particles; they do not establish new independent core-synthesis batches.

source_interpretation.title: Superlattice packing is not atomic crystal phase
source_interpretation.text: The detailed results identify fcc packing of nanocrystals and a (111)s plane parallel to the substrate. The summary instead says normal; the discrepancy is retained. Atomic Au/Ag phase, lattice parameters and coordinates are not supplied by these SEM observations.

source_interpretation.title: Solvent and sonication select different assemblies
source_interpretation.text: Au hexane gives rough mounds, whereas chloroform gives relatively smooth films with triangular step-growth features. The 9:1 hexane/ethanol mixture gives dendritic, nonordered deposits without sonication and faceted superlattice crystallites with sonication during casting. Sonication of good-solvent hexane/toluene dispersions did not produce homogeneous superlattice nucleation.

source_interpretation.title: Temperature affects film morphology, not a reported new core size
source_interpretation.text: Au films from toluene have mounds at room temperature and become flatter but locally disordered at 40°C. Many more defects than in room-temperature chloroform films remain. No new particle size is assigned to this temperature comparison.

source_interpretation.title: Surface diffusion interpretation is model-scoped
source_interpretation.text: The authors discuss bulk diffusion, adsorption, surface diffusion and incorporation or desorption. More attractive interactions and larger supersaturation favor short surface diffusion and radial mound growth; lower supersaturation and longer diffusion favor step growth. The roughly ten-diameter or60nm diffusion scale is an estimate, not measured core or mound size.

source_interpretation.title: SI optical results do not create structural specimens
source_interpretation.text: The SI follows separately prepared Au dispersions in two solvents using absorbance. Final concentrations, elapsed times and fractional losses stay with their optical experiments. Their particle size and exact link to a main-film specimen are unknown. Small short-time changes are interpreted by the authors as insufficient to explain the main solvent-dependent film differences.

source_conflicts: Detailed Results and Abstract describe the superlattice (111)s plane parallel to the substrate; the Summary instead says normal to the substrate. Structured packing follows the detailed Results and the contrary summary remains explicit.

The workup first identifies ethanol as the antisolvent but subsequently prints ethanol/chloroform as the solvent/antisolvent pair. The ordering discrepancy is retained; no silent solvent-role reversal is made.
The general study size range is 5–7 nm, while the specific Ag Figure 1 caption reports 7.2 ± 0.6 nm. The figure-specific value is not truncated to the rounded general range.
SI calls its absorption coefficient molar absorptivity but reports cm2/mg. The source term and mass-specific units are retained without conversion.

SI Equation 2 defines d as center-to-center distance, whereas Figure S1 labels a 25–50 Å separation-distance axis for 6.3 nm particles. No measured spacing or unambiguous center distance is read from that model plot.
limitations: Complete supplied six-page main and matched five-page SI read, including all main Figures 1–6, SI Figures S1–S2, seven SI equations, twenty main numbered references/notes and five SI references. Cited full texts remain unreviewed; independent source audit passed; presentation pending.
Core reaction temperature, atmosphere, vessel dimensions, addition rate and stirring speed are unreported. Stirring windows are retained rather than invented exact times.
Size-selective workup lacks solvent amounts, cycle counts, centrifugation speed and duration. Its printed solvent/antisolvent ordering discrepancy is retained.

Film nanocrystal concentration, individual drop volume, drying duration, substrate pretreatment, humidity and gas flow are unreported. Qualitative ambient/room temperature is not converted to a numeric temperature.

Film assembly uses previously synthesized nanocrystals. Exact batch IDs and preparation-to-figure crosswalks are not supplied; solvent conditions are not asserted to be independent new core syntheses. Au Figures 2A–F explicitly share one size fraction.

Superlattice fcc packing concerns nanocrystal organization, not a measurement of the atomic Au/Ag crystal phase, unit cell or atomic coordinates. Model curves and estimated diffusion lengths are not measured product structures.
Pure ethanol is listed among deposition solvents, but no separately resolved pure-ethanol outcome is supplied. No successful pure-ethanol route is invented.

The SI optical experiment has no reported input-particle size or exact link to a particular main-text film batch. Its dilution volume and post-adjustment mass are unreported; optical changes are not new growth/structure evidence.

Original source figures are proposed only under existing owner-directed display; publisher permission remains unverified. Molecule references and stage drawings are conceptual, with complete presentation pending.
